newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish zloty softens vs basket, depos down.
newsitem.headline: Polish zloty softens vs basket, depos down.

text.p: The Polish zloty softened slightly against the basket of currencies as banks lenghtened currency positions after cutting them on Wednesday to maximize zloty exposure for the week-end, dealers said.
They said the zloty was bound to slowly drift upward to 1.5 percent from parity later in the day as the market's weeks-old light pro-zloty sentiment gains momentum.
"Banks rebuild currency positions in early trade and the zloty eased slightly...but it should be fixed back up at 1.5 percent," said Tomasz Wolosz, forex dealer at BRE bank.
At 0940 GMT the zloty was at 1.47/1.44 percent from the parity rate, weaker than opening's 1.54/1.47 percent.
It was at 3.2335/45 to the dollar, down from opening's 3.2300/20 and at 1.8754/59 to the mark against 1.8750/70.

On the money market one-day rates fell despite a large 1.9 billion zloty combined reverse repo and NBP-bill offer by the central bank on Thursday as banks wanted to place excess cash on the market, dealers said.
"There is a lot of cash out there today as banks are looking to place surplusses before the week-end," said Malgorzata Sikora, dealer at ING Bank in Warsaw.
Overnight rates slipped to 21.95/22.25 percent in morning trade from opening's 22.20/22.40 percent while tomorrow/next rates 22.10/22.30 against 22.25/22.40 percent.
In secondary T-bill trade 270-day paper, sold yesterday at an average yield of 21.48 percent, was quoted at 21.50/21.45.
Dealers said 179-day paper was quoted at 21.47/21.40 flat from 21.44 at yesterday's tender. Foreign investors remained on the sidelines in early Thursday trade.
